GraphQL
GraphQL is a query language and runtime for APIs.
Clients specify the fields they need.
GraphQL commonly exposes a single endpoint.
Queries retrieve data and mutations modify data.
GraphQL can reduce over-fetching when clients need selected fields.

REST API
REST is an architectural style commonly used for web APIs.
HTTP methods include GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE.
GET retrieves resources; POST commonly creates resources.
API responses commonly use JSON.
Example resource endpoints: /users and /products.

Git Branching
A branch is an independent line of development.
git branch creates or lists branches.
git switch changes the current branch.
git merge combines changes from one branch into another.
Feature branches isolate development work.

Git Commands
git init initializes a repository.
git status shows repository state.
git add stages changes.
git commit records staged changes.
git push sends commits to a remote repository.
git pull fetches and integrates remote changes.

Machine Learning Basics
Machine learning learns patterns from data to make predictions or decisions.
Supervised learning uses labeled data.
Unsupervised learning works without target labels.
Classification predicts categories; regression predicts continuous values.
Common models: linear regression, logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, SVM, KNN.

Regression
Regression predicts a continuous numerical target.
Linear regression models relationships between inputs and a numerical output.
Common metrics: MAE, MSE, RMSE, and R-squared.
MAE is the mean absolute difference between actual and predicted values.
RMSE is the square root of mean squared error.

Python Basics
Python is a high-level programming language.
Common data types: int, float, str, bool, list, tuple, set, dict.
Example: name = "Alice"
Functions are defined with def, for example: def add(a, b): return a + b.
Lists are ordered and mutable. Dictionaries store key-value pairs.

Python Exceptions
Common exceptions include TypeError, ValueError, NameError, KeyError, IndexError, and FileNotFoundError.
Use try/except to handle expected runtime errors.
TypeError occurs when an operation is applied to an incompatible type.
Example: len(10) raises TypeError because an integer has no length.

SQL Basics
SELECT retrieves data.
WHERE filters rows.
GROUP BY groups rows for aggregate calculations.
ORDER BY sorts results.
Common aggregate functions: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX.

SQL Joins
INNER JOIN returns rows with matching values in both tables.
LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matching rows from the right table.
RIGHT JOIN returns all rows from the right table and matching rows from the left table.
FULL OUTER JOIN returns matching rows plus unmatched rows from both sides.
Example: SELECT e.name, d.name FROM employees e INNER JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id;
